- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.30) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- If model shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) with negative sentiment, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike (e.g., 3+ days of high prices), model often fails to correct; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% on next day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate late-period prices (last 7–10 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply downward bias of 0.3–0.8% to final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.2–0.6% on day of sentiment shift.
